To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the end-to-end performance of Facebook requests is limited by network latency and the performance of the data center network.

(i) the latency of a request is determined by the slowest component that it touches, (ii) a large fraction of requests are serviced by the slowest components in the system and, (iii) the latency of requests can be significantly reduced by scheduling them in a way that avoids the slowest components.

(i) the latency of Facebook requests is dominated by the time spent waiting for the slowest component to finish, (ii) the slowest component is usually not the one that takes the longest to run, (iii) the time spent waiting is often caused by a small number of components, (iv) the latency of a given component varies greatly over time, and (v) the latency of the system as a whole is not a linear combination of the latencies of the individual components.
